data.title: Epidermal nevus / ILVEN — viva
data.summary: Nevi & hamartomas · 15 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Epidermal nevus / ILVEN** (Nevi & hamartomas)_

**Q1. What is an epidermal naevus?**
- Hamartoma of the epidermis and/or adnexal structures due to postzygotic (mosaic) mutation, following Blaschko's lines; present at birth or early childhood (~1 in 1000)
- Types: keratinocytic (verrucous epidermal naevus — FGFR3, PIK3CA, HRAS; epidermolytic — KRT1/10), organoid (nevus sebaceous — HRAS/KRAS, nevus comedonicus — NEK9, Becker's naevus, porokeratotic eccrine naevus), ILVEN (inflammatory)

**Q2. Describe verrucous epidermal naevus.**
- Linear, skin-coloured to brown, velvety then warty papules coalescing into plaques along Blaschko's lines, usually unilateral on trunk/limbs; localised or systematised (ichthyosis hystrix — bilateral extensive)

**Q3. What is ILVEN?**
- Inflammatory linear verrucous epidermal naevus: persistent, intensely itchy, erythematous, scaly, psoriasiform papules and plaques in a linear Blaschkoid pattern, usually on the lower limb/buttock, onset in early childhood (girls), very resistant to therapy
- Histology: psoriasiform hyperplasia with alternating orthokeratosis over hypergranulosis and parakeratosis over agranulosis; dermal lymphocytes
- Differential: linear psoriasis (responds to antipsoriatics, other psoriasis features, Munro microabscesses), lichen striatus (self-limiting, not itchy), linear LP, linear porokeratosis, linear DLE

**Q4. What is epidermal naevus syndrome?**
- Epidermal naevus with extracutaneous anomalies of CNS (seizures, intellectual disability, hemimegalencephaly), eye (colobomas, lipodermoids), skeleton (hemihypertrophy, kyphoscoliosis, vitamin D-resistant rickets — FGF23 hypophosphataemia), urogenital and cardiovascular systems
- Includes Schimmelpenning (nevus sebaceous), Proteus, CHILD, phacomatosis pigmentokeratotica, Becker's naevus syndrome, nevus comedonicus syndrome

**Q5. Discuss principles of mosaicism (PYQ).**
- Mosaicism = two or more genetically distinct cell populations derived from one zygote (postzygotic mutation)
- Patterns of cutaneous mosaicism (Happle): Blaschko's lines (narrow and broad bands), checkerboard, phylloid (leaf-like — trisomy 13), patchy without midline separation (large CMN), lateralisation (CHILD)
- Type 1 segmental (heterozygous postzygotic mutation in a dominant disorder — segmental NF1) vs type 2 segmental (loss of heterozygosity — severe segment superimposed on generalised disease); gonadal mosaicism → transmission of generalised disease to offspring (e.g. epidermolytic naevus → epidermolytic ichthyosis child)
- Lethal autosomal dominant mutations survive only in mosaic state (Proteus — AKT1, McCune–Albright — GNAS, Schimmelpenning — HRAS)

**Q6. Management.**
- Topical keratolytics, retinoids, calcipotriol, steroids (ILVEN — potent steroids/occlusion, tacrolimus, dithranol) — usually poor response
- Destructive: full-thickness surgical excision (definitive; deep enough to avoid recurrence), CO2/Er:YAG laser ablation, dermabrasion, cryotherapy (recurrence common if superficial)
- Oral acitretin for extensive systematised naevi; examine for associated anomalies

**Q7. Describe the clinical types of epidermal naevi.**
- Keratinocytic: soft (velvety) and hard (verrucous) epidermal naevi, ILVEN, epidermolytic
- Organoid: nevus sebaceous, nevus comedonicus, Becker's naevus, eccrine/ apocrine naevi, porokeratotic eccrine ostial and dermal duct naevus (PEODDN)

**Q8. Clinical features of ILVEN in detail.**
- Onset in infancy/ early childhood, usually lower limb, unilateral, linear along Blaschko lines; erythematous scaly psoriasiform papules coalescing into plaques; intense itch; persistent; female predominance; resistant to therapy (topical steroids, calcipotriol, dithranol, laser)

**Q9. What are the components of epidermal naevus syndrome?**
- Epidermal naevus with CNS (seizures, intellectual disability, hemimegalencephaly), eye (colobomas, lipodermoids), skeletal (bone cysts, hemihypertrophy, kyphoscoliosis), urogenital anomalies; subtypes — Schimmelpenning, nevus comedonicus syndrome, CHILD, Proteus, phacomatosis pigmentokeratotica, Becker's naevus syndrome; hypophosphataemic rickets (FGF23)

**Q10. Differential diagnosis.**
- Linear psoriasis (responds to therapy, later onset), lichen striatus (sudden, self-limiting), linear LP, linear porokeratosis, linear Darier's, incontinentia pigmenti (verrucous stage — girls), seborrhoeic keratosis, warts

**Q11. Malignant potential.**
- Low; BCC, SCC, keratoacanthoma rarely arise in adult epidermal naevi; epidermolytic naevi carry genetic risk for offspring (gonadal mosaicism)

**Q12. Define and classify genodermatoses (PYQ).**
- Inherited disorders with skin manifestations — by inheritance: AD (NF1, TSC, Darier, Hailey–Hailey, EBS), AR (XP, lamellar ichthyosis, PXE, oculocutaneous albinism), X-linked recessive (X-linked ichthyosis, Fabry, Wiskott–Aldrich), X-linked dominant (IP, Goltz, CHILD, Conradi), mitochondrial, mosaic (epidermal naevi, McCune–Albright, Proteus)
- By function: keratinisation (ichthyoses, PPK), adhesion (EB), pigmentation (albinism, piebaldism), DNA repair (XP, Bloom), connective tissue (EDS, PXE, cutis laxa), tumour syndromes (NF, TSC, Gorlin), vascular (HHT), ectodermal dysplasias, immunodeficiency

**Q13. Which genes are involved in epidermal naevi?**
- Keratinocytic (verrucous) epidermal naevus — FGFR3, PIK3CA, HRAS/KRAS/NRAS mosaicism; epidermolytic epidermal naevus — KRT1/KRT10 (gonadal mosaicism → offspring may get epidermolytic ichthyosis)
- ILVEN — GJA1, CARD14 (some)

**Q14. Histopathology of epidermal naevus.**
- Hyperkeratosis, papillomatosis, acanthosis with elongated rete ridges (seborrhoeic keratosis-like); epidermolytic variant shows granular degeneration (epidermolytic hyperkeratosis); ILVEN shows alternating orthokeratosis over hypogranulosis and parakeratosis over agranulosis (psoriasiform)

**Q15. Treatment options.**
- Surgical excision (small), CO2/ Er:YAG laser ablation, dermabrasion, cryotherapy, electrodesiccation — recurrence common if superficial; topical retinoids, calcipotriol, 5-FU, steroids (ILVEN itch), PDT; topical PI3K inhibitors (experimental)

## Quick spotter facts
- Linear warty plaque along Blaschko's lines from birth — verrucous epidermal naevus
- Itchy psoriasiform linear plaque on leg of a young girl — ILVEN

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Epidermal naevi). Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
